questions.question: A hundredths grid is one whole square cut into 100 equal small squares. Maya shades 37 of the small squares. Which decimal names the shaded part of the whole?
questions.explain: Each small square is one hundredth, so 37 shaded squares is 37 hundredths, written 0.37 (two digits after the point). A common trap is writing 0.037, which is thousandths, not hundredths.

questions.question: A hundredths grid is one whole square cut into 100 equal small squares, in 10 rows of 10. Ivy shades 5 complete rows. How many tenths of the whole are shaded, and what decimal is that?
questions.explain: One full row of 10 small squares is one tenth, so 5 full rows are 5 tenths, or 50 hundredths, written 0.5. The trap is counting 5 rows as 5 hundredths and writing 0.05, which would be only 5 tiny squares.

questions.question: A hundredths grid is one whole square cut into 100 equal small squares. Ben shades only 6 small squares. Which fraction and decimal both name the shaded part?
questions.explain: The denominator 100 tells you the whole is split into 100 equal parts, and the numerator 6 counts the shaded ones, so 6/100 = 0.06. The trap is writing 6 hundredths as 0.6, but 0.6 means 60 shaded squares.

questions.question: A hundredths grid is one whole square cut into 100 equal small squares. Sofia wants to shade the grid to show the decimal 0.8. How many small squares should she shade?
questions.explain: 0.8 is 8 tenths, and each tenth is one full row of 10 small squares, so 8 rows means 80 squares (0.8 = 80/100). The trap is shading just 8 squares, but 8 squares out of 100 is 0.08.

questions.question: Ella writes a number as 9 tenths and 4 hundredths. Which decimal is she writing?
questions.explain: The tenths digit goes right after the point and the hundredths digit goes next, so 9 tenths and 4 hundredths is 0.94. The trap is adding 9 + 4 to get 0.13, but tenths and hundredths are different sized parts and cannot be added straight across.

questions.question: Sam and Ana each have their own hundredths grid, and each whole grid is worth 1. Sam shades 7 tenths of his grid. Ana shades 70 hundredths of her grid. Who shaded more?
options: Ana, because 70 hundredths is more than 7 tenths
They shaded the same amount, because 7 tenths and 70 hundredths both cover 70 small squares
Sam, because tenths are bigger parts than hundredths
You cannot compare tenths with hundredths
questions.explain: Each tenth is a row of 10 small squares, so 7 tenths covers 70 small squares, exactly the same as 70 hundredths: 0.7 = 0.70. The trap is thinking 70 must beat 7 without checking the size of the parts.

questions.question: A number line runs from 0.5 to 0.6, and the space between them is split into 10 equal parts. Kai puts a dot on the 4th mark after 0.5. What number is the dot on?
questions.explain: Splitting one tenth into 10 equal parts makes hundredths, so 4 marks past 0.5 is 0.5 + 0.04 = 0.54. The trap is writing 0.504, which puts the 4 in the thousandths place instead of the hundredths place.

questions.question: Leo builds a number with base-10 blocks where one flat is 1 whole, one rod is one tenth, and one small cube is one hundredth. He lays out 15 rods and 3 small cubes. Which decimal shows his number?
questions.explain: Ten rods regroup into 1 whole, so 15 rods are 1 whole and 5 tenths, and the 3 cubes are 3 hundredths: 1.53. The trap is forgetting to regroup the 15 rods and writing 0.153 or 15.3.

questions.question: Ravi and Jade each colour a hundredths grid, and each whole grid is worth 1. Ravi colours 0.5 of his grid and Jade colours 0.45 of hers. Ravi says Jade coloured more because 45 is bigger than 5. Who is right, and why?
options: Ravi coloured more, because 0.5 fills 50 of the 100 small squares and 0.45 fills only 45 of them
They coloured the same amount, because 0.5 and 0.45 both start with a 4 or 5 in the same place
Jade coloured more, because her number has more digits after the decimal point
Jade coloured more, because 0.5 only fills 5 of the 100 small squares
questions.explain: Rewrite both as hundredths before comparing: 0.5 = 0.50 = 50 small squares, which is more than 45 small squares. The trap is comparing 45 with 5 as whole numbers, or reading 0.5 as only 5 squares instead of a full 5 rows.

questions.question: For a class mural at a Burnaby school, Priya uses two hundredths grids side by side, and each whole grid is worth 1. She colours the first grid completely, then on the second grid she colours 4 full rows of 10 plus 5 extra small squares. Which decimal shows how much Priya coloured in all?
questions.explain: Count the wholes first, then the parts: 1 full grid is 1, and 4 rows plus 5 squares is 45 small squares, or 0.45, so the total is 1.45. The trap is ignoring the finished grid and answering 0.45.

questions.question: On a field trip, a hundredths grid stands for one dollar, so each of the 100 small squares is one cent. Aiden shades enough squares to show the 4 dimes and 6 pennies in his pocket. Which decimal names the shaded part, and how many small squares are left unshaded?
questions.explain: Each dime is one tenth, or a row of 10 squares, so 4 dimes and 6 pennies shade 46 squares, which is $0.46, and 100 - 46 = 54 squares stay empty. The trap is writing the dimes and pennies as separate digits, giving $0.406.

questions.question: Lucas shades 3 complete rows of 10 on a hundredths grid whose whole is 1. He writes the shaded amount as 0.03, saying that a hundredths grid always needs hundredths. What should he have written, and why?
options: 0.003, because 3 rows out of 100 squares makes thousandths
0.03, because every hundredths grid answer must have a 0 in the tenths place
0.3, because 3 full rows are 3 tenths, which is the same as 30 hundredths
questions.explain: Count the shaded small squares: 3 rows of 10 is 30 squares, so 30/100 = 0.30 = 0.3. The trap is assuming a hundredths grid can only show hundredths, which turns 3 tenths into the much smaller 0.03.
